symptom: `GRANT … ON Module.Entity` over `--mcp` fails with `failed to read module security for X: GetModuleSecurity: not supported by the MCP backend` — `--mcp-verbose` prints **no PED tool call at all**, and `mxcli mcp capabilities` reports entity access rules as available in the same session. `SHOW MODULE ROLES` / `SHOW USER ROLES` / `SHOW PROJECT SECURITY` fail the same way
cause: The MCP backend embeds `unsupportedBackend` and overrides only what it supports; `gen_unsupported.go`'s own header says it delegates "the reads those [writes] need" — i.e. a read is added **reactively, per write method**. `AddEntityAccessRule` (#704) shipped and was unit-tested, but the executor calls `validateModuleRole` → `GetModuleSecurity` **before** it, and a pre-check made outside the backend package is invisible from inside it. Three reads were missing, not one
insight: **Test the statement, not the backend method** — a unit test on the method passes against a completely unreachable feature, which is exactly how this shipped; drive real MDL through `executor.New` + `SetBackendFactory` against `newFakePED` and assert a `ped_update_document` actually happened. **Probe the whole class**: the reported symptom was GRANT, but the same three-line omission had broken every security `SHOW`, none of which writes anything. **The capability report is a hand-written YAML declaration, not a verified claim** — `capabilities.go` says report and behaviour "cannot drift", and that holds only for the four *method-gated* keys; `entity_access_rules` is a display-only row, so it can and did contradict the very next command. Routing a read to the local `.mpr` is safe **only when PED is not a writer of that document**: roles are by-name references Studio Pro resolves on apply, so a stale file yields "module role not found", never a wrong write — unlike the domain model, which needs the dirty-set router. A module created over PED this session has no security document on disk at all, so answer that case explicitly rather than letting the reader say "not found for module mcp~module~X". Issue #900
